title: Cubane lanthanoid complexes with tridentate [O, P=O, O] coordination using tris(5-tert-butyl-2-hydroxyphenyl)-phosphine oxide ligands: synthesis, characterisation, and magnetic behaviour

synthesis.procedure: LH3 (0.100 g, 0.2 mmol) was dissolved in 5 mL EtOH. HoCl3·6H2O (0.25 mmol) and triethylamine (0.2 mL, 1.4 mmol) were added. The mixture was heated at reflux for 3 h under aerobic conditions with stirring, then cooled, filtered, and left to evaporate in a vial. After 1–2 weeks under ambient conditions, crystals formed; bulk crystalline powder was filtered and washed with cold EtOH and H2O.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aerobic reflux then slow evaporation in a vial
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: cooled and filtered; crystals obtained by slow evaporation; bulk powder washed with cold EtOH and H2O

properties.summary: DC magnetometry of 1 shows room-temperature χMT consistent with four weakly interacting Ho(III) centres and a low-T drop attributed to Stark-level depopulation plus weak antiferromagnetic coupling; magnetisation does not saturate at 7 T/2.65 K and shows no SMT inflection. AC screening at 2.7 K found no frequency-dependent slow relaxation for 1. UV-vis in CH2Cl2 shows a π–π* band at 308 nm.

synthesis.procedure: Same general cubane synthesis as 1–3: LH3 (0.100 g, 0.2 mmol) in 5 mL EtOH with DyCl3·6H2O (0.25 mmol) and triethylamine (0.2 mL, 1.4 mmol), reflux 3 h, cool, filter, and evaporate 1–2 weeks. One coordinated EtOH is replaced by H2O in the crystal of 2. Crystals were obtained directly; bulk powder washed with cold EtOH and H2O.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aerobic reflux then slow evaporation in a vial
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: cooled and filtered; crystals from slow evaporation; bulk powder washed with cold EtOH and H2O

properties.summary: DC data for 2 are consistent with four Dy(III) centres and weak antiferromagnetic coupling; magnetisation does not saturate at 7 T/2.65 K. AC susceptibility shows frequency-dependent in-phase and out-of-phase signals in zero field below 7 K without maxima, so relaxation parameters could not be extracted and QTM is inferred to dominate. UV-vis in CH2Cl2 shows a π–π* band at 309 nm.
